<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable certified canonical KV offloading for `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec` using the existing mapping and scheduler paths. Implements my [claimed cache-type slice](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61886#issuecomment-6217606040) of #61886.

**Depends on #62160.** This branch includes that prerequisite; merge the storage fix first. [Historical GPU-tested feature-only diff](https://github.com/xiaoba17/vllm/compare/a99a46153a3b13034339b32942773b44d0cb651d...3172b52d123acf1bea4f78313089d58354e9ac3a).

## Claims

- Compatible chunked-local and mixed chunked-local/full-attention caches pass the static canonical portability gate.
- Unsupported head configurations, quantization and parallel layouts remain rejected.
- Targeted tests cover cross-TP byte reconstruction, tensor strides/offsets and chunk-boundary store/load behavior.

## Validation

**Current head `5b3db7b397` (2026-11-02)** incorporates #62160's test/docs cleanup. The reduced four-case config matrix covers both full and chunked-local attention; production behavior and FS regression coverage are unchanged. Pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

macOS CPU: **797 passed, 14 skipped, 9 failed** across the seven suites below. The nine failing cases match the saved 2026-10-31 pure-main `7b77ed581d` baseline: six require `/dev/shm`, and three are existing recurrent-event/job-key assertion mismatches. This is not a clean full-suite result. Skips: 11 native FS, one `/dev/shm`, and two unavailable attention-backend cases.

Previous Linux validation at `6b13a95ace`: **751 passed, 2 skipped**, including native `fs_io_C` and O_DIRECT. See #62160 for storage-version isolation and regression sensitivity.

Tests extend existing Buildkite suites.

Linux command below uses the tested host's virtualenv/cache paths. For the current Mac run, the same suites used `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p cpu_only`, with offline OPT config and the existing external `cpu_only` plugin marking accelerator cleanup as unsupported. The plugin does not skip test bodies.

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 PYTHONPATH=.
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HOME=/data/kv-review-hf
export HF_HUB_CACHE="$HF_HOME/hub" HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE="$HF_HOME/hub"
/data/kv-review-py312/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs --tb=short \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

<details>
<summary>Historical dual-GPU validation — commit 3172b52d12</summary>

On 2× RTX 5090, tiny Llama4 (3 chunked-local + 1 full-attention layer, FP16/eager/Triton, chunk size 128, block size 16) passed **10 inference processes**, covering 1/2 KV heads, TP1↔TP2 filesystem reuse, six pressure cycles and a fresh TP1 read after pressure.

| KV heads | Direction | Cold/reload cache-hit contexts | Max absolute logprob delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (replicated at TP2) | TP1 → TP2 | 240/240 in each phase | 0.001486 |
| 1 | TP2 → TP1 | 240/240 in each phase | 0.003836 |
| 2 (sharded at TP2) | TP1 → TP2 | 240/240 in each phase | 0.001499 |
| 2 | TP2 → TP1 | 240/240 in each phase | 0.001481 |

All 512 vocabulary logprobs at 240 teacher-forced contexts were compared with no-offload TP1 references (tolerance 0.005). Prompts straddled chunk boundaries. FS reads and CPU→GPU counters confirmed reuse; after pressure with a 512 KiB CPU cache, a fresh reader hit 240/240 contexts in both phases.

[Historical commands, logs and environment](https://github.com/xiaoba17/vllm/tree/10218a6806b5fff79919eb02fff11c265d2c41de). The custom harness ran outside CI; no new GPU CI job is claimed.

</details>

**Linux native/O_DIRECT and GPU inference have not been rerun at the current head.**

## Details

Only the static certification gate needs production changes beyond #62160: runtime canonical mapping already operates on attention tensors and the scheduler already handles chunked-local windows. Tests verify these paths rather than introducing another mapping or scheduler implementation.

Usage: set `canonical_layout: true` in `OffloadingConnector`'s `kv_connector_extra_config` on every sharing instance. For filesystem reuse use `spec_name: "TieringOffloadingSpec"`, a CPU budget and a shared FS secondary tier as in the archived harness. A focused chunked-local usage section is included in `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`; the broader canonical-layout guide from #61822 is now included in main.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR implements this chunked-local gate extension. #61822 is documentation, #51691 is quantization, and #60782 is a shared-region refactor. Recurrent/Mamba and general filesystem/object-store test infrastructure claimed by others in #61886 remain outside this change.

Limits: random tiny weights establish execution/cache correctness, not trained-model quality or throughput. The sharded model has one near-tied argmax change among 240 contexts in each direction; tolerance passes, but tokenwise/bitwise equality is not claimed. No TP4 GPU, CUDA Graph or multi-node validation. Historical GPU/native extensions used baseline `8e25bbca19`.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and PR preparation. I have reviewed the changes and completed the relevant tests and behavioral validation.

@@ -97,6 +97,20 @@ vllm serve <model> \
 
 Secondary tiers are not supported yet on engines whose workers span several nodes; such an engine fails at startup.
 
+## Canonical Offloading for Chunked-Local Attention
+
+Chunked-local attention (including mixed chunked-local/full-attention models)
+supports canonical KV offloading across compatible tensor-parallel sizes. Set
+`canonical_layout: true` in `kv_connector_extra_config` on every instance sharing
+the cache; the option defaults to `false`. For filesystem sharing, add this
+option to the `TieringOffloadingSpec` configuration in [Multi-Tier Setup](#multi-tier-setup)
+and use the same `root_dir` on the producer and consumer.
+
+Only live blocks needed by the current attention chunk are restored. Canonical
+offloading still requires compatible KV head counts and runtime tensor layouts;
+this support does not enable per-token-head KV quantization or pipeline/context
+parallelism.
+
 ## `kv_connector_extra_config` Reference
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Scope | Notes |
@@ -148,7 +162,7 @@ Enable it on **every** instance that shares a secondary tier. The canonical form
 
 Requirements and limitations:
 
-- Supported layers: full and sliding-window attention whose KV heads divide evenly across TP ranks, and MLA attention. Per-token-head KV-cache quantization isn't supported.
+- Supported layers: full, sliding-window, and chunked-local attention with compatible KV head counts, and MLA attention. Mixed chunked-local/full-attention models are supported. Per-token-head KV-cache quantization isn't supported.
 - Tensor parallelism only: pipeline parallelism, prefill context parallelism (PCP), and decode context parallelism (DCP) are not supported, and the offload workers must be exactly the TP group.
 - Packed and cross-layer KV cache layouts are not supported.
 - If a layer can't be mapped to the canonical layout, the engine fails at startup with an error that says to remove `canonical_layout`, rather than silently storing non-portable bytes.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("form", sorted(CACHE_BUILDERS))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "writer_tp,reader_tp", [(1, 2), (2, 1), (1, 4), (4, 1), (2, 4), (4, 2)]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("total_heads", [2, 8])
+def test_chunked_local_cross_tp_store_load(form, writer_tp, reader_tp, total_heads):
+    """Real derived mappings reconstruct independent KV shards, including replicas."""
+    full_kv = torch.randint(
+        -128,
+        128,
+        (NUM_BLOCKS, 2, 4, total_heads, 64),
+        dtype=torch.int8,
+        generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(0),
+    )
+
+    def physical_pages(kv):
+        # Encode logical [block, K/V, token, head, channel] without copy runs.
+        if form.startswith("packed"):
+            kv = torch.cat((kv[:, 0], kv[:, 1]), dim=-1)
+            if form.endswith("hnd"):
+                kv = kv.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+        elif form.endswith("hnd"):
+            kv = kv.permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+        return [page.contiguous().numpy().tobytes() for page in kv]
+
+    def shards_at(tp):
+        heads = max(1, total_heads // tp)
+        replicas = max(1, tp // total_heads)
+        spec = ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=4,
+            num_kv_heads=heads,
+            head_size=64,
+            dtype=torch.int8,
+            attention_chunk_size=8,
+        )
+        config = _vllm_config(tp=tp, total_kv_heads=total_heads)
+        kv_config = _kv_cache_config([KVCacheGroupSpec(["local"], spec)])
+        mappings, pages = [], []
+        for rank in range(tp):
+            config.parallel_config.rank = rank
+            mapping = derive_canonical_mappings(
+                config, kv_config, {"local": CACHE_BUILDERS[form](spec)}
+            )["local"]
+            assert mapping.parallelism_agnostic
+            mappings.append(mapping)
+            first_head = rank // replicas * heads
+            pages.append(
+                physical_pages(full_kv[:, :, :, first_head : first_head + heads])
+            )
+        return mappings, pages
+
+    writers, writer_pages = shards_at(writer_tp)
+    readers, reader_pages = shards_at(reader_tp)
+    for block_id, expected in enumerate(physical_pages(full_kv)):
+        stored = _store_all(
+            writers,
+            [pages[block_id] for pages in writer_pages],
+            len(expected),
+            block_id,
+        )
+        assert stored == expected
+        for mapping, pages in zip(readers, reader_pages):
+            assert _load_one(mapping, stored) == pages[block_id]
+
+
 def test_cp_round_trip():
     # tp=4 / dcp=2 / 2 KV heads: 4 workers jointly hold one canonical page
     spec = _full_spec(num_kv_heads=1)

+        config = _make_vllm_config(
+            tensor_parallel_size=tp_size,
+            extra_config={"canonical_layout": canonical},
+        )
+        config.use_v2_model_runner = v2
+        assert (
+            build_offloading_config(config, kv_config).parallel.is_parallelism_agnostic
+            is canonical
+        )
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "unsupported", ["heads", "quantization", "mamba", "pp", "pcp", "dcp"]
+)
+def test_chunked_local_canonical_gate_rejects_unsupported(unsupported):
+    """Adding a spec type must retain per-layer and topology restrictions."""
+    spec = ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=16,
+        num_kv_heads=2,
+        head_size=128,
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        attention_chunk_size=128,
+    )
+    config = _make_vllm_config(
+        tensor_parallel_size=2, extra_config={"canonical_layout": True}
+    )
+    if unsupported == "heads":
+        spec = replace(spec, num_kv_heads=1)
+    elif unsupported == "quantization":
+        spec = replace(spec, kv_quant_mode=KVQuantMode.FP8_PER_TOKEN_HEAD)
+    elif unsupported in ("pp", "pcp", "dcp"):
+        axis = {"pp": "pipeline", "pcp": "prefill_context", "dcp": "decode_context"}
+        setattr(config.parallel_config, f"{axis[unsupported]}_parallel_size", 2)
+        if unsupported != "dcp":

+    if unsupported == "mamba":
+        groups.extend(_make_mamba_hybrid_kv_cache_config().kv_cache_groups)
+    kv_config = KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=0, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=groups)
+    assert not build_offloading_config(
+        config, kv_config
+    ).parallel.is_parallelism_agnostic

+    """A static portability claim cannot admit opaque bytes into a shared tier."""
+    spec = ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=16,
+        num_kv_heads=2,
+        head_size=128,

+def test_canonical_fs_upgrade_isolates_legacy_files(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch, layout, family
+):
+    """Rolling-upgrade peers cannot overwrite or delete the other format's files."""
+    new_spec = _canonical_gqa_spec(2, layout)
+    # Reproduce the old TP2 allocation and version without changing FS behavior.
+    old_spec = TieringOffloadingSpec(replace(new_spec.config, canonical_kv_replicas=1))
+    tensors = [
+        _page_aligned_zero_tensor(4, spec.kv_bytes_per_chunk, torch.uint8)
+        for spec in (old_spec, new_spec)
+    ]
+    tensors[0][0].fill_(17)
+    tensors[1][0].fill_(93)
+    tiers = []
+    try:
+        versions = (1, canonical_mapping.CANONICAL_FORMAT_VERSION)
+        for version, spec, tensor in zip(versions, (old_spec, new_spec), tensors):
+            with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+                patch.setattr(canonical_mapping, "CANONICAL_FORMAT_VERSION", version)
+                tiers.append(
+                    FileSystemTierManager(
+                        offloading_spec=spec,
+                        primary_kv_view=memoryview(tensor.numpy()),
+                        tier_type="fs",
+                        root_dir=str(tmp_path),
+                    )
+                )
+        old, new = tiers
+        # Each reader misses the other version's key; both files remain intact.
+        for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
+            tier.submit_store(make_job(i, [key(i)], [0]))
+            results = drain(tier)
+            assert len(results) == 1 and results[0].success
+            assert lookup_and_wait(tiers[1 - i], [key(i)]) == [LookupResult.MISS]
+        for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
+            # Write the same logical key into the other namespace, too.
+            tier.submit_store(make_job(10 + i, [key(1 - i)], [0]))
+            results = drain(tier)
+            assert len(results) == 1 and results[0].success
+            tier.submit_load(make_job(20 + i, [key(i)], [1], is_promotion=True))
+            results = drain(tier)
+            assert len(results) == 1 and results[0].success
+            assert torch.equal(tensors[i][1], tensors[i][0])
+        for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
+            for k in (key(0), key(1)):
+                assert Path(tier.file_mapper.get_file_name(k)).read_bytes() == (
+                    tensors[i][0].numpy().tobytes()
+                )
+        assert old.file_mapper.fields["canonical_format"] == f"v1-{family}"
+        assert new.file_mapper.fields["canonical_format"] == f"v2-{family}"
+        assert old.file_mapper.base_path != new.file_mapper.base_path
+    finally:
+        for tier in tiers:
+            tier.shutdown()

We mapped rolling attention layer matrices to a non-blocking asynchronous eviction loop using native asyncio handles.
